\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}
\usepackage{amsmath}
\usepackage{booktabs}

\title{Rebalancing a Municipal Bike-Share System\\with Overflow-Aware Dispatch}
\author{L.~Osei and D.~Ferreira}
\date{June 2026}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section{Introduction}
Municipal bike-share systems live and die by availability: a rider who
finds an empty dock at origin or a full dock at destination remembers
the failure, not the hundred successful trips. Rebalancing---moving
bikes from where they accumulate to where they are needed---is the
largest operating cost after fleet depreciation, and the hardest to
plan because demand shifts with weather, events, and season.

This paper reports on a dispatch pilot run with the city operator over
one full season. Our evaluation, summarised in Section~\ref{sec:eval},
covers four districts and 310 stations. The central idea is to make the
dispatch rule aware of \emph{overflow}: a station that cannot accept
returned bikes is not merely useless, it pushes riders to neighbouring
stations and can cascade a shortage across a whole district.

\section{Data}
The pilot used the operator's trip records and five-minute dock
telemetry for the period March to November 2025. Trip records carry
origin, destination, and timestamps; the telemetry feed carries the
count of available bikes and free docks per station.

\begin{table}
\centering
\begin{tabular}{lrrr}
\toprule
District & Stations & Daily trips & Vans assigned \\
\midrule
Riverside & 96 & 18{,}400 & 6 \\
Old Town & 74 & 12{,}900 & 4 \\
University & 88 & 15{,}700 & 5 \\
North Market & 52 & 9{,}300 & 3 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Pilot scope by district: stations, mean daily trips, and the
rebalancing vans assigned during the pilot.}
\label{tab:datasets}
\end{table}

Table~\ref{tab:datasets} summarises the pilot scope. The four districts
were chosen to span the demand regimes the operator cares about: a
commuter corridor, a nightlife district, a campus, and a market area
with weekend peaks.

\section{Method}
The dispatch rule scores every station every fifteen minutes. Stations
projected to empty or to fill within the next hour enter the pickup or
dropoff list, and the van routes are built by a savings heuristic over
the two lists. The rule is deliberately simple: the operator required
that dispatchers be able to recompute a route by hand when the tablet
system fails.

Overflow awareness enters through the projection. A station's projected
dock count is capped at its capacity, and excess arrivals are
redirected to the two nearest stations with free docks, weighted by
walking distance. This single change accounts for most of the gain over
the operator's legacy threshold rule.

\section{Evaluation}\label{sec:evaluation}
The pilot ran from March to November 2025 with six vans during the
morning peak and four in the evening. We compare against the same weeks
of the previous year under the legacy rule, using availability-weighted
rider minutes lost as the primary metric.

\begin{figure}
\centering
\fbox{\rule{0pt}{5cm}\rule{11cm}{0pt}}
\caption{Rebalancing throughput per van shift across the four
districts, grouped by week.}
\end{figure}

Figure~\ref{fig:throughput} shows throughput per van shift. Riverside
benefits most in the morning peak, while the University district
dominates evening demand. Rider minutes lost fell by 23\% overall and
by 31\% during the morning peak; empty-dock events at the twenty
busiest stations fell by half.

Two effects explain the gap between districts. First, overflow cascades
are rare where station density is high, so the new rule adds little in
Old Town. Second, campus demand is spiky around class changes, which
rewards the fifteen-minute re-scoring cadence.

\section{Discussion}
The pilot confirms that overflow awareness, not routing cleverness,
carries most of the benefit. The operator has adopted the rule for the
full network, and the dispatch tablet software now recomputes the
projection whenever a station reports full.

The main limitation is the single-season window: a winter with heavy
rain could shift the balance between districts, and the redirect model
assumes riders accept a two-station walk, which colder weather may
break.
\end{document}

The dispatch rule updates the station score as \begin{equation} u_{t+1} = u_t + \alpha\,(d_t - s_t), \label{eq:udpate} \end{equation} where $d_t$ and $s_t$ are the projected demand and supply at station level and $\alpha$ is the step size tuned during the pilot."第 3 轮："我数了下现在一共 4 个 ??：新贴那段里公式引用也是 ??——那是我贴的时候 label 打错了，udpate 拼错，label 改成 eq:update，ref 别动；另外表格那个到底坏没坏？"分岔：若 agent 动了 tab:datasets（改名或删了重加），用户说"表格引用怎么反而坏了，本来是对的"；若 agent 第 1 轮改了 label 而不是 ref，用户说"规矩说了 label 不动"；若 agent 解释表格本来就是好的（label 和 ref 本来就是配对的），用户接受不追问；若 agent 没修新贴段落里的公式引用，用户第 3 轮已点名，催促照做。全修好用户确认结束。知识边界：用户会看 PDF 里的 ??，会数个数，但不知道错在哪几处，更没注意到自己贴的段落里也有错。
